AWAKEN · for your approval · 9 November 2026

Powers in Full Voice

A plan to make using powers the best thing in the game. All 63 judged one at a time: what each does today, what it would do, how it would sound and who had it first. Eight new ones held to a higher bar. And everything around them, from how you get a power to how you read it in a fight.

Nothing here is built. I read the code and measured the sounds, but I haven't played a power or heard a clip. Every verdict is mine from reading, so overrule any of them. The tags say which claims come from the code, which from other games and which are my guesses.

What changed after your notes

  • Clean casts are gone. You were right that a timing window on every power is a layer for the sake of it. Most powers now have no timing at all. Each has a situation where it shines, and that happens by itself. Six keep a moment you can time, because that's what they are.
  • The play styles are spelled out. Section 5 says what being a Kinetic or a Velocity player means and how a family's powers work together. You can still mix them however you like.
  • Passives have their own tab, and all of them are reinvented. Section 6, with a toy of the Aura you described and two new passives.
  • Everything is easier to get. None of the new powers needs the endgame any more, and each has a second way in.
  • The dings are gone from the taster. I measured what you heard. Railgun's launch moment was a single high tone making up over 60% of the sound. All four are remade from real recordings and air. Listen to them.

You were right about the levels. The ladder stays exactly as it is. Three other things hold the powers back:

  • Most are the same wherever you use them. 51 of the 63 are one press and a cooldown.
  • They don't know about the game built since. A power has never filled a boss's stance, and casting isn't part of the Ascent's chain.
  • They sound alike and nobody is behind them. 17 calls to one whoosh, and descriptions that name a path instead of a person.

So the plan keeps the 63 and the ladder and adds ten connected changes: a place where every power shines, powers that count on bosses, combinations you find by experimenting, an R key that fills from how you fight, a ground that really moves, a sound pack per power, and a real person behind each one, ending with your own name on your starter.

You also asked for new powers pushed further than anything there now, and for the whole system to be polished. So there are eight new powers, cut down from eighteen, and each one changes something none of the 63 can touch: your size, time, the road, their moves, sound, the horizon, someone else's body and your own past. And there are seven changes to the system itself, covering how you get, equip, cast, combine, level and read your powers, and how your passives show themselves.

It starts with a playable proof of four powers, and I stop there until you've played it. The new powers come in three waves, with a stop after each.

1What you asked for

Here's how I read it. Tell me if I've got this wrong, because everything below follows from it.

What I took from it
The jobMake using powers extremely fun and satisfying, at every level, for someone who has played a lot.
What's wrongThe first powers were built before most of the game existed and were never revisited. Some are boring. They could be more creative and more technical.
What you want"Holy shit, this is extremely fun and satisfying to use." More progression, more lore.
What you suggestedA sound pack per power, then the powers themselves. I checked whether sound was the main problem. It's one of three.
What you addedNew powers, "really pushed even further" in how enjoyable they are to use and how awesome they look, and "polishing the whole power system up to the maximum". A few astonishing ones beat a long list of decent ones.
What must stayHow they level up. Your saves. Your frame rate. Fair fights.
What I can't checkHow they feel. Only you can do that, so the plan stops early for you to play.

What the bar means, in things you'd notice

StrongWeakUnacceptable
You tell someone about a thing you did with two powers. You could name Railgun with your eyes shut. After a hundred casts you're visibly better and you can hear it. You'd call someone over to see a new power.Bigger numbers, more particles and new sounds laid over the same one press. A new power that's a bigger version of one already there.A power turns into a chore or a quick-time event. Levels you earned vanish. A boss melts in seconds. The frame rate drops. A new power that's only good in a clip.

The success contract

What has to be true
FunEvery power has a better way to press it, and you can tell when you found it.
TruthA power's text says what it does. Numbers come from the simulator, not from me.
EffortNothing to learn before it works. No new menu to manage. A plain cast is today's cast.
ResponseA press answers on the same frame it does today.
ControlYou choose your bar and your Way. The notes can be turned off. Nothing changes your loadout for you.
When it can'tA power with nothing to do does something smaller, or says why and costs nothing.
CostAbout 10 MB of sound. No more frame time than the level 5 limit we already test against.

Not part of this

  • Replacing the six-key bar or the 63 powers
  • Permanent allies or followers
  • A new currency, daily lists or announcing bosses
  • Any new block or item
  • The general frame rate pass, which stays parked

Must not get worse

  • The four named levels and the Awakened form
  • Every level, variant and mastery point already earned
  • The Ascent's movement ladder and Weaves
  • Boss fights: the 20% hit cap and fair damage
  • Cinematic frame time

What other games teach OTHER GAMES

Only for questions that change the design. I read reporting and guides, not the original talks, so treat these as pointers.

QuestionWhat I foundHow far it appliesWhat it changes here
Would a timing reward feel good or like homework?Gears of War made each reload a small timing game with a prize. GMTK notes beginners often ignored it. Testing for the 2026 game moved the bar to mid-screen because that's where people used it most (GamingBolt). Its designer later called the multiplayer damage bonus a mistake (Destructoid headline, the rest of the piece was cut off for me).One repeated action in a shooter. We have 63 different ones.It backs you up. Only six powers keep a moment you can time, and missing it costs nothing.
How many pairings are worth finding?One guide counts 28 Duo Boons in Hades (see Screen Rant and Prima), and Hades II has 37 (Rogue Ranker). Each needs something from both gods.They're rolled per run. You try ours on purpose.24 Duets, each needing only the two powers on your bar.
Rules or a thousand special cases?Breath of the Wild runs a rule-based calculator of states between elements and materials (report on the GDC 2017 talk).An open-world sandbox, and I only read coverage.Six States are general rules. Duets are the named special cases on top.
Can you tell things apart by ear in a busy fight?Overwatch found "the loudest sound wins" and built a system that lifts the biggest threat in the mix, and gave every character its own footsteps (PC Gamer on the GDC 2016 talk).A competitive shooter. I found nothing on how each ability was handled.A mix budget, with your own power and the biggest threat on top.
Timer or meter for the big one?Overwatch fills a meter from damage and healing, with slow passive charge and no timer (wiki, Dexerto).Team PvP. The numbers are community figures.R becomes a gauge, and a slow creep means nobody is locked out.
Fighting beside your own replay: thrilling or a mess?Super Time Force is built on it. Reviewers call it brilliant and also confusing or chaotic (Game Informer, Den of Geek, God is a Geek, GamesRadar).A 2D shooter with many copies at once.Last Time Round is one figure until level 5, in a look you can't mistake for anything else.
How many copied abilities are worth having?Kirby Super Star's team started with more than 40 candidates and kept the strongest (Prima, Nintendo Life). I found no proper design analysis.A much simpler game.I cut hard, and the list of what I cut is on this page.
How long should a press be kept?Smash keeps a press for 9 frames (SmashWiki). Developer blogs give 3 to 5 frames or 80 to 150 ms and warn that long ones feel sticky (Wayline, Bugnet). The sources are uneven.Fighting and action games at 60 frames. Ours is 20 ticks a second.0.15 seconds, which is three ticks. You can try other lengths in section 8.

3Three ways to do it

A. Repair

New sound pack, powers fill stance, end the dead buttons, remove vanilla leftovers.

About 12 hours. Low risk. Decent to good, but the powers are still one press. It fixes what's wrong without reaching what you asked for.

RECOMMENDED

B. Build underneath

Keep the 63 and the ladder. Add the ten changes, polish the system, rework each power by hand on top of them, and add the eight new ones.

About 130 hours, or about 90 without the eight new powers. Each piece can be switched off. It's the only option that reaches the bar and keeps the part you like.

C. Start over

Cut to about 30 deep powers with a new key model.

200 hours or more. Breaks the ladder and everyone's saves. Rejected, though its best idea survives: folding the four Architect shapes into one.

What would change my mind: if Stage 0 doesn't feel clearly better than today's powers, I'd stop and move toward A plus the world and sound work. If the ground wave can't hold your frame rate, I'd cut it back to Swift-style dust and keep the rest.

4How it would work

The ten changes PROPOSAL

1Where it shines: no timing to learn

THE PROBLEM

51 of 63 powers are one press and a cooldown, and nothing about where you use one changes what you get.

THE CHANGE

My first draft gave every power a timing window. You said that sounds like a layer for the sake of it, and you're right, so it's gone. Each power instead has a situation where it's at its best, written by hand and listed on every card below: from high up, in a crowd, in water, on something already Charged. It happens by itself. There's no window, no cue and nothing to learn first. Six keep a moment you can time, because that's what they are: Haymaker, Charged Shot, Railgun, Brace, Dash and Barrier. Missing it still gives you the whole power.

WHAT YOU GET

You get better at a power by learning where to use it, and the fight rewards you for thinking about the fight.

WHAT IT KEEPS

A plain press does everything it does today. Nothing is punished, and nothing asks you to watch a meter.

THE COST

63 situations to write and balance.

HOW WE TEST IT

You play four powers in Stage 0 and tell me. The simulator must show no more than about 12% average gain with every situation met.

2Powers count on bosses

THE PROBLEM

The powers code has zero calls to the stance system. Blades are the only thing that breaks a boss. The one link is an attuned weapon's touch, worth 6.

THE CHANGE

Every power fills stance by weight through the existing Strikes.posture: Light 3, Medium 6, Heavy 12, Massive 20. The same braced and opening rules apply.

WHAT YOU GET

Being a caster finally counts in the fights that matter.

WHAT IT KEEPS

A blade stays the main way. A longsword swung non-stop is about 8 stance a second. A Haymaker every time it's ready is about 3.

THE COST

One more stance source for the boss fights session to allow for. Ranged stance could be abused.

HOW WE TEST IT

combat_sim: breaks per minute no more than 20% above today, tuned on two bosses and checked on bosses it wasn't tuned on.

3No dead buttons

THE PROBLEM

32 places in the catalogue refuse with a red flash: no target 13, blocked 13, and the rest. Dominate and Telekinesis refuse a boss outright, and Gravity Flip skips anything heavy. Worse, a refused cast is normally free, but 14 powers with a wind-up pay first and ignore a later refusal, and at least seven can refuse at that point (Spire, Collapse, Terrain Rip, Thunderclap, Legion, Storm Call, Drone Swarm).

THE CHANGE

An aimed power with nothing to aim at does something smaller. Every power gets a boss version. Wind-up powers check before they charge you.

WHAT YOU GET

A press always answers you.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Real limits stay: energy, cooldown, no room. Those say why and cost nothing.

THE COST

About 30 small behaviours to write.

HOW WE TEST IT

One GameTest casts all 63 at a boss and at nothing. Zero unexplained refusals.

4States and Duets

THE PROBLEM

Seven force reactions exist, mostly against enemy tags, drawn with vanilla particles. Powers barely know each other.

THE CHANGE

Six States show on a creature's body: Lifted, Charged, Burning, Chilled, Held, Read. On top of those, 24 named Duets: two specific powers that make something neither can do alone. You find them by trying things, and they're counted N / ?? like Weaves.

WHAT YOU GET

The stories you tell someone else. Your Well, then your Nova, and the room goes white.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The Weave format, the 20% boss cap, and your freedom to ignore all of it.

THE COST

Stacking is the danger, so every bonus together is capped at about 1.6 times. 24 looks and sounds to write.

HOW WE TEST IT

One test per mechanism. The simulator checks the cap holds in the worst combination.

5Movement powers attack, and casts join the chain

THE PROBLEM

Dash, Leap, Flight, Jet Burst, Snap Cable and others now sit next to the Ascent moves that overlap them. A cast is not a chain link, so the two halves of movement don't know each other.

THE CHANGE

The eight movement powers become attacks that move you. A cast counts as a link in the Ascent's chain, and a long enough chain gives On the Move casts. Wings stay for travel and Flight is for fighting in the air.

WHAT YOU GET

Moving and casting become one thing.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The Ascent's tiers stay the Ascent's. Nothing on its ladder moves.

THE COST

Eight reworks. Chains will reach further, so air fights need a balance check.

HOW WE TEST IT

A test that a cast links through AscentServer.link, and you judge the feel.

6The R key fills from how you fight

THE PROBLEM

Ultimates sit on a 60 second timer. There are seven, six only come from a Path, and four families have none, so R is empty for hours.

THE CHANGE

R becomes a gauge. Your hits, Duets, finishers and kills fill it, and it creeps up on its own so nobody is ever locked out. No energy cost. Your first ultimate is the reward for the D Proving, chosen from what you've actually done.

WHAT YOU GET

The big moment comes when you've earned it, and it comes early enough to matter.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Path signatures still come from Paths.

THE COST

Every ultimate needs rebalancing.

HOW WE TEST IT

Simulator: about 90 seconds of good fighting fills it, about three minutes of sloppy fighting still does.

7The world answers

THE PROBLEM

Almost everything is drawn on top of the world. The tools for more already exist (FxDebris reads real blocks, TerrainLedger restores them, TimeSlow zones) and go mostly unused. Some powers still use vanilla particles, which breaks your look rule.

THE CHANGE

The ground really comes up, in whatever you're standing on. Beam leaves a scorch. Frost freezes real water for a while. The Well pulls loose things and bends shots. Charge runs through water and metal. Flow slows every new sound through the game's own sound event. Every vanilla particle goes.

WHAT YOU GET

It stops looking like an add-on.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Your frame budget. Ground pieces stay inside the existing debris cap (160 full, 64 reduced, 0 minimal). Everything put back afterwards.

THE COST

The hardest look work in the plan. Bending light round a Well would be new Lens work and is only a guess until tried.

HOW WE TEST IT

Stage 0 proves the ground wave first, with FxStats on the Mac.

8A sound pack for every power

THE PROBLEM

172 sound files, and 17 calls to one whoosh. Haymaker and Railgun share a charge. Gravity Well is silent for most of its life. You told me the high dings at the launch moment sound synthetic, and I measured it: 83 of the 172 have a single high ringing tone in their loud part, most of them made by the same few generators.

THE CHANGE

Nothing gets to ring. Every attack is built from real recordings and air, and brightness comes from grit and wind, never from something struck that sings. A check fails any file with a high tone in its loud part, and all 83 get remade. On top of that each power gets a charge or wind, a release, an impact, a tail and a level 5 layer, two versions of each, and each family gets its own materials. A low Choir layer comes in at level 5. A mix budget keeps your own power and the biggest threat on top.

WHAT YOU GET

You could close your eyes and name the power.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Today's sounds. Old files stay in place until you've passed the new one.

THE COST

About 340 sound events and 700 short files, about 10 MB. We have 84 short CC0 recordings and 7 long ones, which is thin, so if it isn't enough I'll come back with a list of more before downloading anything. I can't hear any of them, so your ears are the gate.

HOW WE TEST IT

A listening page per family: Today, New, New in the mix, Keep or Redo on each. Loudness measured to within 1.5 dB, and no file ships with a ding.

9Readings: every power has a person

THE PROBLEM

The descriptions say things like a path's signature or a latent gift. The story already has the answer: the Choir reads people and plays back who they could be. Nothing connects that to your powers.

THE CHANGE

A Power Core is a recording the Choir took of a real person. The Deep is full of people who had them, which is why Lords drop Cores. Each power has a first bearer, one line when you learn it and one more per level. The Journal keeps them in The Choir's Record. At level 5 of your starter you find a second name on the reading.

WHAT YOU GET

Levelling up a power turns into finding out who they were, and then who you are.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The ladder. No Echoes and no allies. The System's plain bracketed voice.

THE COST

About 300 short lines to write and read aloud.

HOW WE TEST IT

You read them all in one file before they ship.

10Progress you earn by playing

THE PROBLEM

Cores come at random by rank, so there's nothing to go looking for, and powers have no tab on the Tasks page. The ladder itself is good, so it stays exactly as it is.

THE CHANGE

Gate themes and Lords lean toward the families they've swallowed, with about a third staying random. At level 5 the System reads how you actually used the power and offers up to three ways to keep it, with the evidence. You pick one and can change it. New Powers tab through Goals.

WHAT YOU GET

You can hunt a power, and level 5 is about you.

WHAT IT KEEPS

All four levels, the 7,000 / 13,000 / 32,000 / 50,000 mastery, and every level already earned.

THE COST

One more choice at level 5, though it's optional and reversible.

HOW WE TEST IT

Ledger and Goals tests. Your Way only uses real counters, so a new player sees no made-up evidence.

The six States

Liftedfrom Kinetic, GravityIn the air and helpless. Any hit slams it down hard for extra stance.
Chargedfrom Charge powersThe next hit arcs to the nearest thing. Water and metal carry it further.
Burningfrom Heat powersA cold hit makes steam. A heavy hit spreads the fire.
Chilledfrom Frost powersThree layers freeze it. A heavy hit shatters what's frozen.
Heldfrom Tethers, grips, ordersIt can't get away. Your next hit lands from the blind side.
Readfrom Mind powersYou can see its next blow. Your next cast on it hits harder and always lands.

The whole system PROPOSAL

The ten changes are about what a power does. These seven are about everything around it, from the moment you pick up a Core.

11Get: having a power should be an event

THE PROBLEM

Right-clicking a Core teaches the power that instant: a bloom, a chord and a window (Powers.useCore). There's nothing to do with it yet. A Core of a power that's already mastered just says so and stays in your hand.

THE CHANGE

Hold use for a second and the Core cracks in your hand. The first Reading plays and the power goes on a free key if there is one. Your first press is free and can't be refused, so you feel it on the spot. A Core of a mastered power can be poured into another power of the same family as mastery.

WHAT YOU GET

Getting a power is a moment, you've used it within five seconds, and no Core is ever wasted.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The same Cores and ladder, sneak-use to swap variants, and the Starter's three cards.

THE COST

A short hold and a crack to make.

HOW WE TEST IT

GameTest: a mastered Core gives mastery and never a level, and the free press spends nothing.

12Equip: your bar should be something you build

THE PROBLEM

One set of six keys (Loadout), so changing build means re-slotting by hand. The card shows cost and cooldown but no damage, and nothing says what a power is good with. Every power sits in one grid of 22-pixel icons.

THE CHANGE

Three saved sets that you name, swapped from the K page or a held key once you're out of a fight. The card gains damage (PowerPreviews already works it out for Cores), where it shines, the Duets you've found, the Reading and a Try button that shuts the menu and gives you one free press. Sort by family, level or what a power does.

WHAT YOU GET

A set for Lords, a set for travel, and a reason to own more than six powers.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Click then press a key, your own bindings, and the ladder on the card.

THE COST

Cooldowns belong to the power and never the set, so swapping can't reset them. Loadout schema 4 carries the sets.

HOW WE TEST IT

A schema 3 save loads as set one. Swapping during a fight is refused.

13Cast: stop throwing presses away

THE PROBLEM

A press a moment before the cooldown ends is refused and forgotten (ClientCasting.press). The reason appears in small type beside the hotbar with no sound. Nothing shows where an area power will land.

THE CHANGE

A press buffer: in the last 0.15 seconds of a cooldown or during another power's wind-up, your press is kept and fires the moment it can. Hold the key on the dozen or so powers that land somewhere to see where, with a ring in the power's own look, and let go to cast. A tap still casts at once. The reason moves to your crosshair, once a second, with a low thud that differs for no energy, not ready and no room.

WHAT YOU GET

Powers stop eating your inputs, and you know where the big ones will land.

WHAT IT KEEPS

A tap is the same as today. Movement prediction and second presses are untouched, and the six held powers keep hold as their charge.

THE COST

A buffer must never fire something you've changed your mind about, so any other power key or a dodge clears it.

HOW WE TEST IT

GameTest: a buffered press fires once and spends once. You judge the feel at Stage 2.

14Combine: help you play the Duets you've found

THE PROBLEM

Powers combine in seven small ways that nothing on screen shows (ForceInteractions). The plan adds States and Duets, and the screen has to keep up.

THE CHANGE

When a creature has a State that one of your keys can use in a Duet you've already found, that key shows a small glint. Duets you haven't found never show. The first time you find one, the moment slows for a quarter of a second and its name goes up once, large. States sit on the creature's body and on its lock-on panel, and a party member's count too.

WHAT YOU GET

You can play Duets on purpose once you've found them, and finding them stays a surprise.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The N / ?? list, and the rule that nothing tells you what you haven't found.

THE COST

A few more small things on the bar, so they only show in a fight.

HOW WE TEST IT

A test that an unfound Duet never sends a glint.

15Level: leave it alone and add a little

THE PROBLEM

You like this and you're right to. In a fight it's a short sting and the moment waits. When it's calm you get the bloom, a chord and a window naming the step (Evolution), and the slot's frame grows. Two gaps: you can't see mastery while fighting, and the window tells you about the new step without letting you feel it.

THE CHANGE

Everything stays. The window gains a Try It press: your next cast of that power is free and shows the new step. When you're a few uses from the next level, the slot's frame draws a thin line round itself. The window also carries the next line of the Reading.

WHAT YOU GET

The moment you level up, you get to use what you just earned.

WHAT IT KEEPS

All of it: the steps, the frames, the sting and the moment, and mastery thresholds.

THE COST

Almost nothing.

HOW WE TEST IT

A test that Try It is free once and only once per level.

16Read: you should be able to fight without looking down

THE PROBLEM

The bar is 20-pixel slots beside the hotbar, a long way from where you're looking. A cooldown is a dark shade that shrinks, and when it ends nothing happens at all, no flash and no sound. Energy is a 3-pixel bar. Slot edges stay grey unless a power is running.

THE CHANGE

A slot that comes back gives a bright glint and a quiet tick pitched to its family, and a full R gets a bigger one. The cooldown becomes a bright sweep you can catch from the corner of your eye. Family colours on every edge. A ghost on the energy bar shows what your last press cost. Two thin arcs at the crosshair for energy and R, only during a fight, with a setting to turn them off.

WHAT YOU GET

You know what's ready by hearing it.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Frames that grow with level, the beating outline for a second press, F1 hiding it all, and the narrow-screen layout.

THE COST

Clutter is the risk, and you approved Clear Screen for a reason. So nothing near the crosshair shows outside a fight, and it has to fit with the aim dot (SPEC 40.5).

HOW WE TEST IT

CI tour shots at your MacBook's size, then you play.

17Always On: passives you can see, read and switch

THE PROBLEM

Four passives. Every one you own runs four times a second with no way of stopping it. On the K page they come last in the list with a 3 pixel dot, and at level 1 Aura is a faint flash and Wall Stride is nothing at all.

THE CHANGE

Their own tab on the K page, one row of icons on the Tab glance, and Full, Quiet or Off on each. Every passive shows and sounds from level 1, always tells you it was you, and the System names it the first time it acts. Section 6 has all of it.

WHAT YOU GET

You always know what you've got, what it's doing and that it was you.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Every level and mastery point, and the name and meaning of every step on the ladder.

THE COST

A new tab, one more row on the Tab panel and one more saved field. Another session is working on the Tab panel now, so that row goes in after it.

HOW WE TEST IT

A GameTest for each state and for refusing a change in a fight. CI shots of the tab at your MacBook's size.

The rules it must keep

StepWhat happens
TriggerA key press on one of the six slots, exactly as today.
ReadsThe power, its level and variant, your aim, what's under your aim, your movement, what's already on the target, your energy and cooldown.
DoesSecond press? Can it act, and which version? Pay. Wind up. Release. Hit, stance, State. Duet check. Gauge, mastery, counters.
You seeThe effect, the State on the creature, and the first time you find a Duet, a toast.
AllowedDamage and stance inside the caps, temporary terrain through the ledger, short-lived summons.
SavedLoadout schema 4 only, with your sets. Nothing mid-fight is saved.
When it can'tNo energy, on cooldown, no room: it says why and costs nothing.

These are always true

  • A plain press does at least what it does today
  • The server decides damage, never the client
  • The 20% boss hit cap stands, and all bonuses together stop at about 1.6 times
  • Every terrain change puts itself back unless it's something you built
  • No permanent allies, only short-lived summons and decoys
  • No power moves, stops or controls another player
  • With a change's setting off, the game behaves as it did without it

When two things clash

  • Boss cap beats the 1.6 cap, which beats any single bonus
  • Two time effects: the stronger one wins, they never stack
  • A Duet needs both powers from you or your party
  • The Ascent's ladder always wins over a power that overlaps it
  • A kept press is cleared by any other power key or a dodge

Saves and data

WhatWhereOld saves

Readings you've seenWorked out from your level, not savedEarlier lines appear in the Journal straight away.
States, ground piecesMemory onlyNever saved. A relog clears them.

Recordings, road points and held hitsMemory onlyNever saved. A relog clears them.

AI: not applicable. There's no AI in this feature.

Multiplayer and boundaries

  • The server is in charge, and looks and sound stay on the client
  • Duets work across a party
  • Dominate, Echo Swap and time stop never touch players
  • The existing limit on aim-bending against people stays
  • Bonuses for where a power shines don't apply against players
  • Other people see your Aura, and a setting turns other people's passives down if a crowd gets busy
  • Stormborn's bolts never strike another player, and Second Shadow never hides you from one
  • None of the eight new powers can stop, grab or enter another player
  • No new data leaves the game

Frame rate and cost

  • Limit we already test against: level 5 costs at most 0.5 ms typical and 1 ms worst over level 1
  • Ground pieces stay inside the existing cap
  • About 10 MB of sound on top of the current 2.2 MB
  • A command prints how often each power is used, Duets found and stance dealt
  • Titan and the Clock add no meshes. Road Ahead is a drawn strip with no block changes. Toll uses the screen pass power impacts already have. The Long Cut is the only new power that changes many blocks
  • The Aura mantle is one more pass of a body that's already being drawn, simpler on Swift and past about 24 blocks, and tested with ten players before it's built out
  • Frame tests run on your Mac when it's quiet, under slot.sh

5Play styles

You said the kinds of power should feel like they work together, and that it should be clear what it means to be a Kinetic player or a Velocity player. Today a family is a coloured edge and one word on a card. The K page sorts by it, and nothing says what it's for SEEN IN CODE. So each of the nine becomes a way of fighting you can recognise and choose. You can still mix them however you like.

KINETIC

Up close and heavy

You want to walk up to it and hit it until it's somewhere else.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You start close and stay close. Shockwave or Ground Slam throws them in the air, Haymaker sends the biggest one through a wall, and Brace stops whatever comes back.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
Most of these leave things Lifted, and the rest hit Lifted things hard, so every power sets up the next one.
GOES WELL WITH
Velocity, for the run-up: a Shockwave at the end of a Dash is Sonic Stamp. Shadow, for the surprise: charge a Haymaker, Shadow Step, and that's Knock Knock.
Heavy Hands: Things you knock into the air stay up half a second longer.
VELOCITY

Never where it lands

You want to be gone by the time the blow gets there.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You keep moving. Dash through the hit, leave an Afterimage carrying on where you were, and when it gets bad, Flow slows the whole room down.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
These all pay you for what you do on the way past. Standing still wastes them.
GOES WELL WITH
Kinetic, for something to land: Sonic Stamp again. Energy, for what you do in slow time: Flow and Beam make Slow Burn.
Never Still: While you're moving fast, your powers come back 10% sooner.
FLIGHT

Above it

You want the fight to be happening underneath you.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You get up high and stay there. Gravity Well pulls them together, Telekinesis picks up the one that matters, and Meteor Dive finishes it.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
Gravity powers gather things up and air powers get you over them. Anything pulled together is waiting for something big to land on it.
GOES WELL WITH
Energy, for the big finish: a Nova inside a Well is Collapsing Star. Tech, for the angle: a Railgun through a Well is Slingshot.
Good Air: Powers you cast in the air cost 15% less energy.
ENERGY

Stand back and light it up

You want to stay well back and make the room very bright.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You keep your distance and spend big. Beam wears things down, Charged Shot picks off what's coming, Barrier holds the line and Nova clears whatever gets close.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
Energy powers leave things Charged, and Charged things set each other off. It all adds up to Overload.
GOES WELL WITH
Flight, to bunch them up: Collapsing Star. Mind, for a nasty surprise: a Decoy that goes off as a Nova is Surprise Party.
Full Tank: Your energy refills 15% faster when you haven't been hit for three seconds.
SHADOW

Get there first

You want the fight to be over before it knows it started.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You pick the moment. Cloak to get close, Shadow Step behind the one that matters, and Echo Swap out when it turns round.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
Every Shadow power is about being somewhere they didn't expect, and your first hit is always your biggest.
GOES WELL WITH
Kinetic, for one enormous hit: Knock Knock. Flight, for a dirty trick: swap something into your own Well and that's Switcheroo.
First Blow: Your first hit on something that hasn't noticed you does 25% more.
MIND

Knows what you'll do

You want to know what it's going to do, and then decide what it does instead.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You watch first. Read Intent shows you the next blow, Foresight shows you a boss's, Dominate turns the big one on the others and Decoy gives them something else to hit.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
Mind powers leave things Read, and everything else you've got hits a Read target harder.
GOES WELL WITH
Velocity, to use what you saw: Dash through a blow you read and that's Already Gone. Energy, for Surprise Party.
Two Steps Ahead: Anything you've Read stays Read for two seconds longer.
ARCHITECT

Bring your own ground

You want to decide what the place looks like before the fight starts.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You get there early and change it. Blueprint for cover, Rampart for a fort, Spire to throw things up and Collapse to bring the roof down on them.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
Everything you build is something your other powers can use: to stand on, hide behind or drop on someone.
GOES WELL WITH
Tech, to man the walls: a Turret on a Spire is Crow's Nest. Energy, to use them: a Beam through your own wall is Prism Wall.
Home Ground: Within six blocks of something you built, you take 10% less damage.
TECH

Let the machines work

You want things that keep working while you do something else.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You set up, then you aim. A Turret on high ground, a Drone after whatever you just hit, the Railgun for the big one, and Grapple for when it goes wrong.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
Your machines fire on what you hit, so every cast counts twice.
GOES WELL WITH
Architect, for somewhere to put them: Crow's Nest. Velocity, for a second shot: your Afterimage firing the Railgun again is Two Shots.
Well Maintained: Your drones and turrets last 25% longer.
SPIRIT

An answer for everything

You want to be hard to kill and to have something for every situation.

A FIGHT LOOKS LIKE
You carry a bit of everything. Spirit Palm up close, Cord Lash to tie them together, Bulwark when it gets bad, Mend when it's over, and fire, frost or a storm for whatever's in the way.
HOW THEY WORK TOGETHER
It's the widest family: body and soul, heat, cold and storms. Those set each other off, so Ember Step through something Chilled makes steam.
GOES WELL WITH
Kinetic, for the one-two: Spirit Palm inside a Haymaker is One-Two. Energy, to protect people: a Mend into your Barrier is Sanctuary.
Still Standing: Your heals and shields are 15% stronger.

Lean in, or mix

The bonus on each card above is a Style. Put three powers of one family on your six keys and you get it, and a passive of that family counts as one of the three. With six keys you can hold two Styles at once. If you mix everything you get no Style, but you have the most Duets on offer. Neither is the wrong way to play. Style bonuses sit inside the same 1.6 cap as everything else PROPOSAL.

All in on Kinetic

Six of one family. You get Heavy Hands, and everything you've got sets up everything else.

Three and three

Half Kinetic, half Velocity. You get Heavy Hands and Never Still, and Sonic Stamp is right there.

One of everything

No Style at all, and the most Duets to find. Also a perfectly good way to play.

Where the game would say this

WhereWhat it shows
The starter choiceOne plain line for each of the three on offer, so your first pick is a choice of how you want to fight.
K, PowersThe family's name, its one line and how many you have on your keys, at the top of each family's group. Sort or filter by family.
Every power's cardA Works With line: other powers in the family that set this one up, and any Duets you've already found.
The power barA small family mark at the end of the bar while a Style is active, so you can see you've got it.

6Always On

You asked for passives to have their own tab and for every one of them to be pushed as far as it can go. And you found the real problem by playing: you had Aura on, things round you were taking damage, you couldn't see why, and there was nowhere to check what you owned.

What's there today SEEN IN CODE

PassiveWhat you can see and hear at level 1Can you turn it off?
AuraA small quiet flash on what it hits, and a few faint motes once a second. No sound of its own.No
Danger SenseA red glow and a quiet ping. It's the only one you can really read at level 1.No
Wall StrideNothing. Its look only starts at level 2.No
Water RunThe game's own splash particles.No

Every passive you own runs four times a second and nothing can stop it (Casting). On the K page they come last in the list with a 3 pixel green dot, clicking one does nothing, and the only description is the card that shows when you hover (PowersSection). Aura also hits anything hostile in reach, and each hit puts you in combat, so it can start a fight you were walking past.

Five rules every passive follows, from level 1

  1. You can see it and hear it at level 1. Steps on the ladder add to what it does. They never unlock the fact that you can tell it's there.
  2. When it acts, you know it was you. A line runs from you to whatever it touched. The damage number is in the family's colour with the passive's small mark on it. Its icon flares at the end of your power bar.
  3. The first time it ever acts, the System tells you. Once, in plain speech. "[That was your Aura. It hits anything that gets too close. You can look it up under K, Always On.]"
  4. You choose how much of it you want. Full, Quiet or Off, on the tab. Quiet keeps the part that matters and drops the show.
  5. It stays out of the middle of your screen. Nothing crosses your crosshair. Shapes are capped, and it's simpler on Swift and past about 24 blocks.

And one line of lore that holds them together: a power is one moment someone had. A passive is something someone did every day.

Where you see them: both places, doing different jobs

K, Always On is the one place with everything. The Tab glance is the quick look in the middle of doing something else. Mockups, with real icons and made-up numbers.
