ALWAYS ON

One new row on the Tab panel. Lit means it's on. Bright means it acted in the last few seconds. Dim means Quiet or Off. You only get the row if you own a passive. Another session is working on the Tab panel right now, so the row goes in after it lands.

Turning them off

You asked whether they can be deactivated, and it's decision 29. I'd say yes: Full, Quiet or Off on each one, changed on the tab. It's refused in a fight, so it can't be used as a trick. Off means off: no effect, no look and no mastery earned, and an Off passive doesn't count towards a Style. It saves with your powers, and an old save starts with everything on Full. A separate setting turns down other people's passives if a crowd gets too busy.

Try the Aura

Move your pointer around: that's the creature. Bring it close and the mantle stands up and leans at it. Get it within reach and a tongue goes out, bites and comes back with a bright bead. Try each level, and switch to What You See for how it looks from your own eyes. It's silent, and it's a drawing of the idea, not the game.

Level 1. It works from the very first rung.

YOUR SOUL

Aura

Spirit · passive · decision 30

Your soul doesn't fit inside you any more.

A living mantle of jade fire wraps your actual body. It isn't particles floating near you. It follows your shoulders, your arms and the line of your head, it streams behind you when you run and it flattens when you land. Every two seconds a tongue of it peels away from you, goes for something in reach, bites, and comes back carrying a bright bead that sinks into your chest.

TODAY

1.2 damage every two seconds to whatever hostile is within 3 blocks. A small quiet flash on up to three of them and a few faint motes. No sound of its own. Wisps only arrive at level 2. You had it on and things were taking damage from nowhere.

AT REST

Low and slow, like breathing. A thin line of light round your body and a lick or two at the shoulders.

WHEN SOMETHING COMES NEAR

Something hostile within about 10 blocks and it stands up. It gets taller and leans toward the nearest threat like a flame in a draught, so it tells you where to look.

WHEN IT ACTS

The tongue. One for each target, up to three drawn, a beat apart so they read as separate strikes.

FROM YOUR OWN EYES

Never in the middle of your view. Licks rise past the bottom corners and curl round your hands. A tongue starts beside your hand and thins as it leaves, so it's gone before it reaches your crosshair.

WHAT OTHERS SEE

The whole figure. It's your Path's colour once you have one. It frays and gutters when you're nearly dead and burns tall when your R is full, so anyone who looks at you can read how the fight is going.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A low temple drone that only comes up when something's near. Each tongue is a soft indrawn breath and a knock when it lands. The bead coming back is one soft low pulse in your chest. There's nothing high or bright in it, and all of it sits under everything else in the mix.

HOW YOU KNOW IT WAS YOU

A line of light from you to the thing it hit, every time. The damage number is jade with a small Aura mark on it. The first time it ever strikes, the System says what that was, once.

WHERE IT SHINES

Stand still for one second in a fight. The mantle gathers up, and the next strike goes out as a whole arm of light that hits twice as hard.

ON A BOSS

Light hits that take a little stance. A tongue on a boss stays attached for a moment, so you can see it's doing something. The 20% cap still applies.

QUIET AND OFF

Quiet keeps the tongues and a thin edge of light and drops the mantle. Off stops it: no damage, no healing, nothing to see.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Crouch and it pulls in tight and stops striking, so it can't start a fight you were sneaking past. Today it can: it hits any hostile in reach, and each hit puts you in combat. It never touches pets, villagers or other players. Damage at level 1 is what it is today.

Lv 2 · WispsWisps break off the mantle and circle you in a fight. Its reach grows by a block.
Lv 3 · CalmOut of a fight the mantle goes bright and still, and you heal twice as often.
Lv 4 · DragA tongue holds on for a moment before it lets go, and whatever it held is slowed.
Lv 5 · Soul GuardHit you up close and the whole mantle turns on them at once.
[Everyone has this. Most people just call it being in a room with someone.]
SEEN IN CODE EnergySwirlLayer, the way the game draws a charged creeper, is a second pass of a body's real model with a scrolling texture. We already add our own layer to every player skin (MuzzleLayer), first-person arms have their own hooks (FirstPerson.view, Hands), and a tongue is the existing TETHER shape from you to a target.
MY GUESS How a glow that hugs the model looks under Lens and shaders, and what it costs with several players wearing it. One short test before the rest gets built.
About 5 hours, with its sound, ladder and tests.
YOUR NERVES

Danger Sense

Mind · passive · decision 31

You flinch before it happens.

The blow draws itself in the air before it lands. A thin line, the exact path of the claw, the blade or the arrow, shows up the moment the creature commits to it. A rush of air swells in the ear it's coming from. Get out of the way at the last moment and the line snaps, the world's sound drops out for half a beat, and the thing that missed is left open.

TODAY

Anything about to hit you glows red, with a quiet ping. The arc at the edge of your screen only comes at level 2. It's useful and it's the best of the four, but it's still an outline on a creature.

AT REST

Nothing at all. No glow and no sound. That's the point: when this wakes up, it means something.

WHEN SOMETHING COMES NEAR

When something commits to you, the edges of your view cool by a shade.

WHEN IT ACTS

The path of the blow, the note in the right ear and, if you dodge, the miss.

FROM YOUR OWN EYES

The line is in the world, so it's exactly where the blow will be. Only the line and the note. Nothing new sits on your crosshair.

WHAT OTHERS SEE

Your eyes light pale gold for a moment before the hit lands. From outside it looks as if you knew.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A rush of air that swells in the ear it's coming from, deeper for a Heavy and with a low growl under it for a Perilous. There's no beep. The miss is a soft thud with everything else ducked under it.

HOW YOU KNOW IT WAS YOU

The line only exists because of this power, and a gold ripple comes off you when a dodge pays off.

WHERE IT SHINES

Move as late as you dare. The later you step out, the more energy you get back and the longer the thing that missed stays open.

ON A BOSS

Reads a boss's tells, never sooner than the boss's own wind-up starts. It tells you where. The fight still decides when.

QUIET AND OFF

Quiet keeps the note and the arc and drops the line. Off is nothing at all.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Only blows aimed at you, and at most the nearest two lines at once. Anything with no move data gets today's red glow, so nothing is lost.

Lv 2 · Edge ArcAn arc at the edge of your screen points to threats you can't see.
Lv 3 · SoonerThe line and the note come 0.2 seconds earlier.
Lv 4 · Read the ShotA drawn bow shows you the whole flight of its arrow, in gold, before it's loosed.
Lv 5 · Sixth SenseA dodged blow slows whatever threw it for a second, and the world takes a full beat.
[Hester Pike flinched eleven seconds before the bridge fell. Her whole family crossed it on a different day because of that.]
SEEN IN CODE Told blows already have their wind-up and reach in the boss kits (KitMoves), SLASH already draws a blade's arc, danger marks already go to the one player (PowerPayloads.Marks), and dodges are already detected and paid (Mastery.DODGED).
MY GUESS Whether lines read in a crowd. It has to be seen in a real fight, and if they don't, Quiet's note and arc become the default.
About 3 hours, with its sound, ladder and tests.
YOUR FEET

Wall Stride

Velocity · passive · decision 32

Nobody told you walls were for stopping.

Walls become road. Sprint beside one and your hand goes out and drags along it, throwing sparks off your fingers. On the wall your feet leave prints that burn red and fade. The run stays white for as long as anyone could have held it, then turns red at the moment only Wall Stride is keeping you up, so you can see exactly what it's giving you. Come off the end and all of that speed goes into whatever you do next.

TODAY

Your wall-runs last four seconds. At level 1 nothing shows that at all: its look only starts at level 2.

AT REST

Sprint within arm's reach of a wall and your free hand trails along it.

WHEN SOMETHING COMES NEAR

On the wall: burning footprints, dust shaken loose behind you.

WHEN IT ACTS

The wake turns red past the normal length. Leaving the wall throws a red ring behind you and carries the run's speed into your next hit or cast.

FROM YOUR OWN EYES

Your hand at the edge of the view, sparks running back past you and the horizon leaning over. Nothing near the crosshair.

WHAT OTHERS SEE

Someone running flat along a wall with a red line burning behind them.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A quick patter of soles on whatever the wall is made of, climbing in pitch with the length of the run.

HOW YOU KNOW IT WAS YOU

The moment the wake goes red, it's the power holding you up.

WHERE IT SHINES

Cast or strike as you come off the wall. You get the whole run's speed, and the hit knocks them the way you were running.

ON A BOSS

Nothing of its own. It feeds your next hit, and a boss room with pillars becomes somewhere to build speed.

QUIET AND OFF

Quiet keeps the red at the end of the run and drops the prints. Off puts your wall-runs back to their ordinary length.

KEEPING IT FAIR

The Ascent's wall-run stays the rule, and this only extends it.

Lv 2 · Spark StepsSparks kick off each step, and you get half a second longer on the wall.
Lv 3 · Kick-offLeaving the wall gives you a burst of speed.
Lv 4 · SteadyA thin red line marks your path along the wall, and you don't sink at all.
Lv 5 · Street RunnerA red ribbon trails you, you flip off the end, and each new wall within a second of the last adds a second.
[Nobody told Ines Cardo that walls were for stopping you. She was four, and they never managed to explain it to her afterwards.]
SEEN IN CODE RunnerRules already knows the run with and without it, so the colour change is one number. StepHooks.strideTick already sends a look every viewer sees and only needs its level check removed. anims.client.Hands already moves your arms in first person.
MY GUESS Whether the hand reaching out feels natural. It only ever uses a free hand.
About 3 hours, with its sound, ladder and tests.
YOUR WEIGHT

Water Run

Velocity · passive · decision 33

The sea is just another road.

A real wake. It fans out behind you, rolls outward and lasts for several seconds, so you can look back and see where you've been. At full speed sheets of spray stand up on either side of you. Stop dead and the whole wake catches up with you and breaks forward past your feet in a low wave that knocks over and soaks whatever's in front. And at level 5, run straight at a waterfall and you keep going, up it.

TODAY

Sprint and you run on the water. At level 1 it throws the game's own splash particles, which breaks your rule about vanilla looks.

AT REST

Stand at the water's edge and the surface leans toward your feet in small ripples.

WHEN SOMETHING COMES NEAR

The first step onto the water rings out from your foot.

WHEN IT ACTS

The wake, the spray and the hard stop.

FROM YOUR OWN EYES

The horizon rocks a little with your stride and spray comes in low at the edges of your view.

WHAT OTHERS SEE

A long white V across a lake with somebody at the point of it.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Slapping sheets of water that climb to a steady hiss as you speed up. The hard stop is one heavy slap and a long wash running out.

HOW YOU KNOW IT WAS YOU

You're standing on a lake.

WHERE IT SHINES

Hit the water at a sprint out of a jump without breaking stride. Then stop hard with your enemy in front of you.

ON A BOSS

Not a fight power. Anything the wave soaks counts as wet for Charge.

QUIET AND OFF

Quiet keeps the running and a thin white line. Off means sprinting swims again, which today you can only get by holding crouch.

KEEPING IT FAIR

The wave pushes and barely hurts. The waterfall only works on real falling water with room above it.

Lv 2 · WakeNo slowdown as you step onto water, and the wake widens.
Lv 3 · SkipA leap off the water keeps your speed, and each stride leaves a ring of light.
Lv 4 · Still WaterYou can stand on water for two seconds, and it stills in a circle under you.
Lv 5 · TidewalkerYou run up waterfalls, and at full sprint you throw a bow wave.
[Jory Wake's boat sank a mile out. He says he didn't want to get his boots wet, and nobody can tell if he's joking.]
SEEN IN CODE It's already client physics with a server check (ClientCasting.waterRun), so a waterfall is one more case. Foam is a drawn ribbon on the surface, the same as Road Ahead, with no block changes.
MY GUESS Whether foam drawn on the surface holds up at shallow angles and beside Water Edges. One short test.
About 4 hours, with its sound, ladder and tests.
YOUR SHADOW

Second Shadow

Shadow · passive · new · decision 34

Your shadow stopped copying you.

Your shadow has its own ideas. It's a beat behind you when you move. It's a little too long. When something hostile is near, it turns its head before you do. Stand somewhere dark for two seconds and you go unlit: the shadow comes up round your feet, your steps stop making a sound and creatures have to be much closer to notice you. The first blow you land from the dark, a black arm comes up out of the ground a moment ahead of your own.

TODAY

Doesn't exist. Cloak is the only stealth power, and it's a press.

AT REST

In daylight, just your shadow being slightly wrong.

WHEN SOMETHING COMES NEAR

Near something hostile it turns to look at it. In the dark, that's sometimes the only way you'll know where they are.

WHEN IT ACTS

Going unlit, then the arm.

FROM YOUR OWN EYES

You see it on the ground ahead of you when the light's behind you. When you go unlit the edges of your view sink a shade and your own footsteps fall away.

WHAT OTHERS SEE

A shadow that doesn't match. In the dark, someone they can't quite make out.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Your footsteps fade out over half a second when you go unlit. The arm is a very low wet thud and a breath you can't place.

HOW YOU KNOW IT WAS YOU

The black arm comes up out of your own shadow.

WHERE IT SHINES

Stay unlit until they're within arm's reach. The closer the first blow, the harder the arm hits.

ON A BOSS

Once a boss is fighting you it can't lose you. You get one arm at the start, if you arranged to start from the dark.

QUIET AND OFF

Quiet makes your shadow behave and keeps going unlit and the arm. Off is a normal shadow and normal footsteps.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Only real darkness counts, and a torch ends it. Anything already chasing you keeps chasing you. You're never invisible, and other players see and hear you as usual.

HOW YOU GET IT

Land five first blows from the dark, with no light in your hands. Or find its Core in any gate that leans Shadow.

Lv 2 · InkGoing unlit takes one second instead of two.
Lv 3 · HushCreatures that lose sight of you in the dark forget you twice as fast.
Lv 4 · Long ReachThe arm can come up out of any shadow within 6 blocks of you.
Lv 5 · Both of YouFor three seconds after the arm, your shadow stands up and fights beside you.
[Marta Voss kept a lighthouse alone for thirty-one years. She always laid two places for dinner, and the relief keeper says both plates were clean.]
SEEN IN CODE LivingVisibilityEvent is the game's own hook for how visible you are, and light level is one call. A flat copy of your real model is one more render layer.
MY GUESS A flat copy of your body on uneven ground. If it looks wrong on slopes I'll say so, and the arm and going unlit stay while the shadow goes.
About 5 hours, with its sound, ladder and tests.
THE SKY

Stormborn

Energy · passive · new · decision 35

Lightning likes you now.

In a thunderstorm the lightning starts finding you. A bolt comes straight down on your head and you stand there lit up and unhurt, with a full energy bar and your hands crackling. Your next cast goes out overcharged. Hit something while you're crackling and the sky finishes the job. Storms become the thing you go outside for.

TODAY

Doesn't exist. No passive cares what the weather is doing.

AT REST

In clear weather, a tick of static off your fingers when you open an iron door.

WHEN SOMETHING COMES NEAR

In rain the drops turn to sparks just before they reach you, and you feel thunder in your hands before you hear it.

WHEN IT ACTS

The strike, every twenty to forty seconds in a storm, always with half a second of warning: a hum, and a line of light on the ground at your feet.

FROM YOUR OWN EYES

Your hands crackle at the bottom of your view. The strike whites out the edges, never the middle.

WHAT OTHERS SEE

A person being hit by lightning on purpose.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A rising hum through the floor, the crack right on top of you, and a long fizz that fades as the charge does.

HOW YOU KNOW IT WAS YOU

You've just been struck by lightning and your energy bar is full.

WHERE IT SHINES

Stand still under the warning with an empty hand. Move and it lands beside you and you only get half.

ON A BOSS

Only in a storm, so it rarely matters in a gate. Outdoors in a storm, the sky can land on a Lord, under the usual cap.

QUIET AND OFF

Quiet keeps the strike and drops the sparks in the rain. Off and lightning goes back to ignoring you.

KEEPING IT FAIR

The bolts are drawn, not real, so they never start fires, touch your builds or turn a creeper. Other players are never struck by it.

HOW YOU GET IT

Stand outside in a thunderstorm with an Energy power on your bar. The sky picks you out within a minute or two, and that first bolt gives it to you. Or find its Core in any gate that leans Energy.

Lv 2 · GroundedA bolt can take your energy over its maximum for ten seconds.
Lv 3 · Long FuseYou stay charged twice as long.
Lv 4 · ForkedThe bolt forks into whatever's near you.
Lv 5 · Eye of ItFor as long as the storm lasts, every hit you land while charged brings a bolt.
[Arlo Finch was struck nine times and kept all the hospital receipts. After the fourth he started going out in storms. His wife says he liked being noticed.]
SEEN IN CODE EntityStruckByLightningEvent and the storm check are already used in the mod (WorldLatents, Bells). A drawn bolt is the existing LIGHTNING effect, which can't set anything alight.
MY GUESS How often a storm really happens in a normal session. If it's too rare, the bolts need to start in ordinary rain.
About 3 hours, with its sound, ladder and tests.

What didn't make it, and why

I tried a passive for every family and cut the ones that weren't good enough on their own.

IdeaWhat it would doWhy it's out
A hero landing (Kinetic)Every fall ends in a three-point crouch and a crack in the ground.The Ascent's slam already owns landing.
Wind at your back (Flight)The air around you moves with you and pushes you along.There's no wind to read, and it's the Ascent's job again.
Ground that rises to your foot (Architect)Stones lift to meet your step on a slope.Road Ahead does this properly.
A drone on your shoulder (Tech)A small machine that follows you and helps out.That's a permanent ally, and you've said no to those.
Full hands (Energy)Your hands glow brighter the fuller your bar is.It's a nice touch but not a power. It's folded into how the bar reads.

7Eight new powers

You asked for new powers pushed further than anything in the catalogue, both to use and to look at, and you said a few astonishing ones beat a long list of decent ones. I agree. So I wrote down what a new power has to do, came up with eighteen, and kept the ones that passed.

The test each one had to pass

1
Nothing else does it

It has to do a kind of thing the catalogue doesn't do at all. A bigger version of something we already have doesn't count.

2
You'd call someone over

One moment you'd want to show another person, and it has to look as good from outside as from inside.

3
The hundredth time is better

You get better at it. A power that's at its best the first time you press it fails.

4
It belongs here

It comes from something the story already says, and you get it by doing something the world can remember.

5
It can really be built

The parts exist in the code or a short named test can prove them, and it stays fair, safe for multiplayer and inside the frame budget.

The eight that passed don't overlap. Each one changes something none of the 63 can touch:

Your sizeTitanTimeStopped ClockThe roadRoad AheadTheir movesSay It BackSoundTollThe horizonThe Long CutSomeone else's bodyBorrowed BodyYour own pastLast Time Round

Where each one comes in

YOUR SIZE

Titan

Kinetic · Ultimate, on R · wave 1

The R key is full. You grow, as big as the place allows, up to five times your height: nine blocks on open ground. For twelve seconds your swing sweeps a whole room, Z is a stomp that sends the ground out in a wave, and X picks up anything smaller than you and throws it.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

The fight changes scale in a second. The thing you were dodging is at your waist. You can feel your weight: every step rocks the camera and throws up real dirt, and the trees you walk through go down.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Nothing else in the catalogue changes your size. It's also the only power that gives your other keys new jobs while it lasts.

HOW IT LOOKS

You stay yourself, armour and all, only huge, with hot orange seams at the joints. The growth comes in three heaves. Your shadow falls across the ground ahead of you and mobs look up.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A creak like old timber taking load as you grow. Sub-bass footsteps you feel more than hear. Your own breath and your own power sounds drop about an octave while you're big, and come back up when you shrink.

WHERE IT SHINES

Start growing in the middle of a group. The first stomp lands on all of them at once.

ON A BOSS

A boss can't be picked up. X shoves it instead and takes a big bite of stance. Every hit still stops at the 20% cap.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Other players are never grabbed. In a cave or a gate you only grow as far as the roof allows, and if a roof closes in you shrink to fit, so you can't get stuck.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Offered at the D Proving if most of what you've done with powers so far is Kinetic. Anyone else: a Core from any gate that leans Kinetic, and a Kinetic Core is guaranteed after three gates of that kind.

Lv 2 · Longer StrideYou cover ground at the speed your legs look like they should.
Lv 3 · UprootedX can tear up a tree or a boulder and throw that.
Lv 4 · Walking EarthquakeEach step ripples the ground and trips small things near your feet.
Lv 5 · The Whole HeightAwakened. Seven times your height on open ground, and the first stomp cracks the land out to 30 blocks.
[Bram Okoye was five foot two and lifted a bus off a child outside Carillon station. He weighs a lot more in the Choir's copy than he did in life. So will you.]
SEEN IN CODE The game's size attribute goes up to 16 times and we already use it on mobs (MobScaling). Step height, reach and jump are attributes too.
MY GUESS How the camera and first-person arms behave at five times size. One short test.
About 3 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
TIME

Stopped Clock

Velocity · Ultimate, on R · wave 1

One tick of a clock, then nothing. Every creature near you stops dead, the colour drains out of the world and only you and your own powers keep theirs. For three seconds you walk around a fight that's holding its breath. Arrows hang where they were. Everything you do is held: your shots leave your hand and stop a metre out, and your hits pile up on whatever you struck. Then the clock starts again and all of it lands in the same instant.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

It's three seconds of planning inside a fight, and then one enormous payoff that you built. You walk round a frozen boss laying shots around it like a firing squad. The better you compose those three seconds, the bigger the one frame at the end.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Flow and Foresight slow things down. This is the only power where what you do waits, so you're stacking up a single moment instead of hitting things in turn.

HOW IT LOOKS

On your screen every creature freezes mid-step, animation included. Held shots stay lit and slowly turn. A thin white mark appears for each hit waiting on a target. On release: one frame of white, then full colour comes back all at once.

HOW IT SOUNDS

The tick. Then almost nothing: the whole mix drops to a low hum and your footsteps are the only clear thing. Each held hit adds one quiet note to a rising stack. On release the stack and every impact play as a single hit with a long tail.

WHERE IT SHINES

Stop the clock with a lot of things around you. Everything you do in those three seconds lands together, so a crowd is where it's biggest.

ON A BOSS

Bosses don't stop. They drag at a quarter speed so a fight stays a fight. All your held hits on one boss count as a single hit for the 20% cap, and the release is worth Massive stance.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Other players never stop. A held hit is dropped if its target has left the area. If you die or log out, nothing is held any more and the world starts again.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Offered at the D Proving if you mostly fight with Velocity powers. Anyone else: take Flow or Foresight to level 3. You've spent long enough in slow time that one day it stops.

Lv 2 · Another SecondFour seconds, and you can hold one more shot.
Lv 3 · Pushed AsideSlap a hanging arrow or bolt and it goes where you sent it when the clock restarts.
Lv 4 · Everything At OnceHeld hits also set off any State on the target, all together.
Lv 5 · NoonAwakened. Six seconds. Rain stops in the air, and for a second after the release nothing near you can cast.
[Yusra Demir mended clocks. When the Choir asked her what she wanted, she said one more minute with the shop open. She's still in it. It's still that minute.]
SEEN IN CODE TimeSlow already cancels creatures' ticks near you. The client has its own freeze switch (TickRateManager), and the renderer already honours it for every creature, so only you see the full stop.
MY GUESS Vanilla particles and rain aren't covered by that switch. Our own effects can hang. The rest needs trying.
About 4 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
THE ROAD

Road Ahead

Architect · Movement, on Left Alt · wave 2

Hold Left Alt and start running. A strip of hard light lays itself down in front of your feet, tile by tile, wherever you're looking. Run off a cliff and it carries on. Look up and it climbs. Lean into a turn and it banks. It stays behind you for ten seconds and then falls away in pieces.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

It's a line you draw across the sky with your own body. There's speed to build on the way down and speed to lose on the way up, so a long run is a real piece of driving. You can jump off it, drop, and land back on your own road further along.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Every other way of moving is a burst or a hover. This one is continuous and you steer it, and it leaves something behind that's still there when you look back. Other players can run on it too.

HOW IT LOOKS

Warm blueprint gold. The tiles snap into place with a small overlap, so it reads as something being built very fast. The edges glow where you've just been and cool as they age. At the end of its life each tile drops and rings off the next.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A ratchet that clicks once per tile and speeds up with you until it blurs into one rising note. Creaks on the tight bends. A wooden boom as you pass twice sprint speed.

WHERE IT SHINES

Come off the end of the road with speed and land on a ledge or a creature. The speed carries into the Ascent's next move.

ON A BOSS

Lay it round a boss and you can stay out of reach, but a hit needs a landing. Coming off the end onto a boss is a drop attack that counts your speed.

KEEPING IT FAIR

It costs energy for every second you're climbing, less on the flat and none going downhill. Run out on the way up and the tiles ahead flicker for a second before you drop, so you always get a warning.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Reach the top of an Elder Colossus or a Lumen Spire, any way you can. The Core waits in the cache beside the crown.

Lv 2 · BankingNo speed lost in the turns.
Lv 3 · Two LanesWide enough to turn round on, and a friend can keep up beside you.
Lv 4 · KerbSmall creatures that touch it get tripped.
Lv 5 · The Long RoadAwakened. It stays for thirty seconds, and going downhill pays energy back.
[Pia Lund carried the post on foot between the hill towns. In the last winter she got tired of waiting for roads. There's a line of frost across the pass that still hasn't melted.]
SEEN IN CODE Water Run already holds you up with client physics, and the Runner's hang already passes the game's floating check. A road is a list of points plus a drawn strip, with no block changes at all.
MY GUESS Whether it feels like driving or like sliding on glass. That's the whole power, so it gets its own test.
About 4 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
THEIR MOVES

Say It Back

Mind · Active, on Z X C or V · wave 2

When a boss or Lord throws a big move at you and you dodge it, deflect it or read it cleanly, this key takes a copy for fifteen seconds. Its icon changes to show what you've got. Press it and you do that move: its shape, its reach, its colours and its own sound, from your own hands, aimed where you're looking.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

The biggest thing in the room just tried to kill you with it, and now it's yours. Every boss gives you something different, so this power plays differently in every fight you'll ever have.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

It's the one power whose content comes from the enemy: 497 moves across 47 bosses, 47 of them signatures. It's also the answer to Fights That Read You. They read what you've started. This lets you read them back.

HOW IT LOOKS

The copy is made of glass in the boss's own colours. A blow comes out as a huge glass limb the size of the boss's own, swinging from your shoulder through the real arc of the move. A ring of bolts is the boss's own bolts. A slam is its own crater, lit from inside.

HOW IT SOUNDS

The move's own sound, taken up three semitones and dried out. You recognise it instantly, and it sounds like a bad impression of the thing that scared you.

WHERE IT SHINES

Say it back while the boss is still recovering from the original. It staggers harder.

ON A BOSS

The damage is yours, worked out from your own level and never the boss's. A boss hit by its own signature takes double stance and can't use that move again for 20 seconds.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Moves that make no sense in your hands get a translation: a summon gives you one short-lived copy of yourself, a guard gives you a perfect guard for a second, a heal heals you a little. It never copies another player.

HOW YOU EARN IT

The first time you dodge or block a Lord's big move, at any rank, the System offers it.

Lv 2 · Long MemoryIt holds a copy for thirty seconds.
Lv 3 · Two at OnceIt holds two moves on one key, and each press spends the oldest.
Lv 4 · Word for WordSignature moves come out at the boss's full size.
Lv 5 · Say It FirstAwakened. If a boss starts a move you've said back before, pressing now beats it to the punch, cancels its move and takes a huge bite of stance.
[Ines Okafor could repeat anything she'd heard once, in the voice she heard it in. Mostly she used it to win arguments with her mother. The Choir read her for eleven minutes, and she read it back.]
SEEN IN CODE Every boss move is data (KitMoves): hit shapes, timing, sounds and what kind of ability it is. The 25 ability kinds are a fixed list (Ability.Kind), so one set of player versions covers every boss.
MY GUESS More than half the moves (265 of 497) are body blows, so the glass limb has to look right. One boss in a test will show it.
About 5 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
SOUND

Toll

Spirit · Active, on Z X C or V · wave 2

You strike the air with your open hand. Every sound in the world drops away. Half a second later a bell goes off that's bigger than anything you've heard in this game, and you can see the sound leave: a thin gold ring going out across the land, through hills, out past where you can see. The Deep's creatures reel. And any bell you haven't found that's within earshot answers, faintly, from where it is.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

The silence first. Then the size of it. You stand on a hill and watch a ring cross the valley, and then from somewhere out there you hear one small note come back.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

It's the only power that's as much for the map as for the fight, and the only one where the sound is the weapon. It also ties straight into the game's main goal.

HOW IT LOOKS

A hair-thin gold ring that bends the view as it passes, shakes dust off every surface it crosses and lifts the birds. An answering bell shows as a small ring on the horizon in the right direction.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Built from the real recorded bells already in the game, low and heavy. The silence is the existing muffle system taken nearly all the way down, so the first thing you hear is your own hand landing.

WHERE IT SHINES

Strike near a real bell. Yours takes its sound and goes out twice as far.

ON A BOSS

Deep and Hollow bosses take Massive stance and lose their next move. Everything else takes a Medium hit to stance. The Deep can't stand it, and the rest just don't like it.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Reach runs from 60 blocks at 50 bells up to 200 at 100. A setting keeps the silence from being total for anyone who finds it uncomfortable, and subtitles give the direction of an answering bell.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Ring 15 of the Hundred. It comes from the bells themselves, and its reach grows with every one you ring after that.

Lv 2 · CarryingThe answering bell is louder, and you can tell how far away it is.
Lv 3 · Held NoteHold it and the silence lasts three seconds. Nothing caught in it can cast.
Lv 4 · Second StrokePress again as the ring fades to send a second one.
Lv 5 · Full PealAwakened. Three strokes, and every bell you've rung within reach sounds along with them.
[Marta Selby rang the noon bell in Carillon for forty years and was late exactly once. She was on the stairs when the bells stopped. She's still on the stairs.]
SEEN IN CODE Bells.count gives your number. Soundscape.muffle already takes the world's sound down for dreams. A screen-bending pass already exists for power impacts (FxScreen).
MY GUESS How far out the ring still reads. Far Sight's distant land may hide it.
About 4 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
THE HORIZON

The Long Cut

Energy · Ultimate, on R · wave 2

Hold R. A hair-thin white line draws itself across the ground from your feet to as far as you can see, following the land over hills and across valleys. You can sweep it left and right. Let go and for half a second nothing happens. Then the land opens along that line, from your feet to the horizon, in one travelling wave. Anything on it is cut. Trees drop in. Over the next half minute it closes again, from the far end back toward you.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

You changed the view. From a hilltop you can see the whole of what you just did, a straight line through everything for 200 blocks. The half second of nothing between letting go and the land opening is the best part.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

The longest reach any power has today is 48 blocks. This one reaches the horizon, and its effect is the landscape.

HOW IT LOOKS

A cut three blocks wide and up to twenty deep. The inside walls glow like cooling steel and steam comes off any water that falls in. Near you the blocks are really gone. Far away it's drawn on the land as a dark seam with hot edges, which costs almost nothing.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A rising rush of air that stops dead. Half a second of nothing. Then a tearing sound that starts at your feet and travels away from you, and the far end reaches you late, the way thunder does.

WHERE IT SHINES

Let go when the line has reached full length. It goes as far as you can see.

ON A BOSS

One Massive hit and Massive stance, only if the line crosses it, inside the 20% cap. Worth aiming.

KEEPING IT FAIR

It never touches anything anyone has built, any village, or any block that can't be put back. In a gate the floor holds and you get the line of damage with no canyon. Everything comes back on its own, even after a crash.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Finish any Lord at rank B or above with an Energy power on your bar, and it hands you its Core.

Lv 2 · Steady HandA wider sweep while you hold.
Lv 3 · Second LinePress again to cross it with another.
Lv 4 · Deep CutCreatures caught in it are stuck for two seconds.
Lv 5 · Both WaysAwakened. It goes out in front of you and behind you at once.
[Tomasz Ilyin was told to draw a line on the map to show where the evacuation would stop. He had a Halo gun and a bad sense of humour. Nobody crossed that line for nine years.]
SEEN IN CODE TerrainLedger takes blocks out and puts them back, even after a crash, and refuses protected ground. Real blocks only within about 40 of you, spread over a second. Soundscape.muffle does the silence.
MY GUESS The frame cost of even that many block changes on your Mac. And whole trees: you told me nothing should float, so a cut tree has to go down in one piece.
About 5 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
SOMEONE ELSE'S BODY

Borrowed Body

Mind · Ultimate, on R · wave 3

Press R looking at a creature. Your body kneels where it stands with its eyes shut, and you're inside the creature. You walk on its legs at its height. Left click swings what it swings, and Z, X, C and V are its own moves. Press R at another creature and you jump across, and the one you left falls over.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

You get to be the monster. A ten-block beast rampaging through its own friends, then you hop to the thing on the roof that was about to shoot you. Chaining hops through a whole room is the skill, with your real body waiting, helpless, somewhere behind you.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Everything else changes what your character does. This changes who your character is. No other power hands you another creature's height, speed and moves.

HOW IT LOOKS

A thin pink thread runs from your kneeling body to the creature's head, tighter and brighter the further you go. The camera drops or rises to its real eye height. The creature you're wearing has a pink light where its eyes are.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Your own breath, small and far behind you, under the creature's heartbeat and all its real sounds right up close. When your body is hit you hear it from the wrong direction.

WHERE IT SHINES

Hop into the biggest thing there. When the one you're in dies, you keep the time you had left, plus two seconds.

ON A BOSS

You can't get into a boss. Press R at one and you reach in for a moment: it drops its next move and stumbles a step.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Twelve seconds at most. Your real body can be hit, and one hit pulls you back. You can't go further than 48 blocks from it. Never other players, and never anyone who lives at your Hearth. Kills count for half the mastery.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Give 25 orders with Dominate. You've been telling creatures what to do for long enough that one day you go in yourself.

Lv 2 · Better FitSixteen seconds.
Lv 3 · Quick HandsA hop costs no time at all.
Lv 4 · Someone WatchingYour kneeling body gets a dome that takes the first hit.
Lv 5 · Full OccupancyAwakened. Whatever you were last inside keeps fighting for you for ten seconds after you leave.
[Ren Takeda looked after other people's dogs. He could tell you exactly what one was about to do. The Choir found out why, and then nobody could find Ren. Keep your own body somewhere safe.]
SEEN IN CODE Handing the camera to another entity is already done for the opening, the Forge and the map (setCameraEntity). The moves of every boss-grade creature are data. Dominate already takes creatures over through Allies.
MY GUESS This is the riskiest of the eight. Driving a creature by hand instead of by its brain hasn't been tried here. It gets its own test, and if that's poor I'll say so and drop it.
About 8 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
YOUR OWN PAST

Last Time Round

The Signal · Ultimate, on R · wave 3

Press R. The last eight seconds of your fight are pulled out of you. A white figure with gold seams and no face stands up where you were eight seconds ago and does exactly what you did: the same steps, the same powers, at the same moments, at 60% strength. Meanwhile you're free to do something else.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

You get to fight beside yourself, and you can plan for it. Set up a Well, throw a punch, press R, and spend the next eight seconds doing what your past self couldn't. When your old Well meets your new Nova, that's a Duet, and you played both halves.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

It's the only power whose effect is whatever you just did. Play well and it's devastating. Play badly and you get to watch yourself do it again. It can't be the same twice.

HOW IT LOOKS

The same body as the Last Loop, at your size. Just before it stands, the path it's about to walk lights up from the far end as a thin gold line, exactly as the boss did it to you. Every power in its hands is white and gold instead of its family's colour, so you never mistake it for yourself.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Your own sounds, half a step lower and with a long tail, arriving very slightly late. A low tick counts off the eight seconds.

WHERE IT SHINES

Use it at the end of your best eight seconds. The figure does exactly what you just did, so the better the eight seconds, the better the figure.

ON A BOSS

Real damage and real stance at 60%, inside every cap. Bosses can't read it, because it isn't deciding anything.

KEEPING IT FAIR

It repeats what your powers did. It never builds, never summons and never moves land. Only one at a time until level 5, and it can't record itself.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Beat the A Proving. It kneels, lays its blade down and leaves you this. The Last Loop, at the very end, gives it its last step.

Lv 2 · Ten SecondsTen seconds of you instead of eight.
Lv 3 · Step BackPress R again while it's out and you swap places with it, wherever it's got to.
Lv 4 · Word for WordThe figure hits at full strength.
Lv 5 · Every Time RoundAwakened. Two figures: the last eight seconds, and the eight before.
[That was you. You got further than this once, and everything you've got, you brought back with you. There's no other name on this one.]
SEEN IN CODE The Last Loop boss already keeps your path, a sample every two ticks. EchoGhost already walks a recorded path wearing your skin. Power hits run through one place (Combat.hurt) and effects through another (Fx), so the figure repeats the results and never has to re-run 63 powers' code.
MY GUESS Whether repeating results looks right when the target has moved. A test with four powers will show it.
About 5 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.

Play with the strangest one

Last Time Round is the hardest one to picture, so here's a toy of it. Move around, hit the boss, then press the button. Everything you did in the last eight seconds comes back and plays beside you, so whatever you do next is on top of it. This is only a drawing of the idea. It isn't the game.

Move, click at the boss, then press this (or R).

The older powers

The same goes for the 63 you already have. Nothing gets harder to find than it is today. Random Cores stay, and a Gate Lord still guarantees one if you've gone three bosses without. On top of that, gates start leaning toward the families they've swallowed, and a leaning gate's Core is one you don't have yet whenever there's one left in that family. Today a Core knows nothing about what you own. Your first ultimate comes at D instead of from a Path, and Paths still give their own.

What didn't make it, and why

Two of these were in my first draft of this plan. Say if you'd have any of them back.

IdeaWhat it would doWhy it's out
Nobody HomeIn my first draft. For six seconds nothing near you remembers you're there.Cloak already does nearly this. It's a good trick, and it isn't a new kind of thing.
Second TryIn my first draft. Go back to where you stood four seconds ago with the health you had then.Last Time Round says the same thing better, and its Step Back level gives you the best part. Rewinding health sits badly with fair damage.
UnderSwim through solid ground and come up beneath someone.The game resets a player's collision every tick, and a camera inside stone is a rendering job of its own. Lovely, and too much risk for now.
OrbitLock on to a boss and circle it like a moon, faster and faster, then fling off.A great feel, and better as a level 5 Way for Gravity Well than as its own power.
Two DoorsPlace two linked doors and send anything through.Without seeing through them it's half the idea, and a live view through a door is too much for your frame rate.
Down Is Over TherePick any wall and make it your floor.The game's physics knows up and down and nothing else. It would mean rebuilding how the player moves.
EclipseCover the sun and fight at midnight in the middle of the day.Looks wonderful, but underneath it's a colour grade and a damage buff. Better as Legion's Awakened look.
Thousand CutsThe world stops and you flash through everyone with camera cuts.Hundred Palms and Lightning Step already own this.
CometGo up out of sight and come down as a meteor.The Ascent's Judgement Fall is this, and the rule is that the Ascent's moves stay the Ascent's.
Second WindAt zero health you get six seconds to earn it back.It muddies fair damage and the way dying already works in gates and dreams.

Dov Harlan

Learned[Dov Harlan threw one punch in his whole life that mattered. The Choir kept a copy of it. That's what you're holding.]
Level 2[He was a dock worker. The man he hit was the foreman who'd been shorting everyone's pay.]
Level 3[The foreman lived. Dov went to prison for it, and the docks paid everyone what they were owed the next week.]
Level 4[He never threw another punch. When the Choir asked him why, he said he hadn't needed to.]
Level 5[I looked at this reading again. There are two names on it. His, and under that, yours. You picked this one last time too.]

That last line appears only on the power you chose as your starter. It agrees with what the story already says: the Signal is you, from an earlier loop.

LEVEL 5: YOUR WAY, FOR A HAYMAKER

[I've been watching how you use this. There are three ways it could go from here. You can change your mind later.]

Listen

I can't hear these. I only measured them, so you're the judge. You said the dings, the high sounds at the launch moment, sound super synthetic. So I built a check for exactly that, and it found them: in my first Railgun a single 2,089 Hz tone was over 60% of the sound at the moment it fired, and 83 of the game's 172 power sounds have the same thing.

Each power now has three clips. Today is rebuilt from the real files, at the moments the code plays them. Remade has nothing in it that rings: it's real recordings of an electric arc, wind, thunder, stone falling and a far explosion, plus punches and air. What I took out is only the layers I removed, on their own, so you can tell me if that's the sound you meant. My check only looks above 800 Hz, so on some clips it finds nothing high, including two of the takings-out, which are low struck tones. If you still hear a ding on a clip marked no high tone found, tell me: that means my check is missing what you can hear. All of them are evened out to the same loudness, so you're comparing the sound and not the volume. Each wave is drawn to scale. Headphones if you can.

Every power, one at a time

Tick Not this one on anything you'd change. The verdicts come from reading the code, so overrule me freely. The line in the box is what the System says when you learn the power.

Kinetic

7 powers

Sounds like: stone and sub. Where the readings come from: The waking body. Ordinary people who found out what they could move.

Ground Slam
Active
Flat
Today

A ring of damage round you, 4.5 blocks. From the air you dive first, up to +14 damage for height. Shockwave and the Leaper's slam now do most of this, and nothing about it says ground.

After

The real ground answers. The blocks round you kick up in a ring and roll outward, drawn from whatever you're standing on, so sand and stone look and sound different. From high up it leaves a crater for ten seconds. Whatever the crest catches is left Lifted.

Where it shines
Come down on something from high up. The higher you start, the bigger the crater and the further it throws them.
On a boss
Heavy stance hit, more the further you fell.
Sound
A dropped wall: a sub thud first, then a drum roll of blocks travelling away from you. The surface changes the top layer: gravel hiss, sand sigh, stone crack.
[Tomas Reyne worked a pile driver for thirty years. When the Choir read him it found he'd stopped needing the machine.]
Leap
Movement
Flat
Today

A big forward bound with a small blast on landing. The Ascent now gives you double jumps, dives and slams, so this mostly repeats them.

After

A hunting leap. Hold to crouch and a landing circle shows up to 24 blocks out. Let go and you arrive there, already striking. It counts as a link in your movement chain, so it joins the Ascent instead of competing with it.

Where it shines
Leap at something from a long way off. The further the jump, the harder you land on it.
On a boss
Medium stance, doubled if you land in an opening.
Sound
Knees creak, a ground thump as you leave, wind that rises and falls with the arc, then a landing body-thud.
[Nadia Orrin was late for a ferry and she made it. The ferry was already a quarter of a mile out.]
Haymaker
Active · Starter
Keep and polish
Today

Hold to one second, let go, reach 4.5; a whiff throws a ring. The best idea in the family, because you can feel the wind-up. Its charge sound is the same file the Railgun uses.

After

Keep it and polish it. Hold to build and let go whenever you like. At full charge time hitches, the target folds, flies and cracks the wall it lands against.

Where it shines
Let go as it reaches full charge and time hitches, the target folds and it cracks the wall behind. Hold for as long as you like: a late punch is still a full punch.
On a boss
The biggest stance hit of any starter.
Sound
In the taster. Knuckles and a straining shoulder climbing to a thump at the peak, torn air, meat and stone, a long sub drop.
[Dov Harlan threw one punch in his whole life that mattered. The Choir kept a copy of it. That's what you're holding.]
Terrain Rip
Active
Good, needs a hook
Today

Tears up to nine real surface blocks out and throws them straight away, and the hole fills back in. A strong idea that's over in one quick press.

After

You keep the torn-up chunk over your head while you aim, with a line showing where it lands, and the blocks grind against each other as you hold it. Press again in flight to burst it.

Where it shines
Rip it up in a corridor or a cave, where the chunk has nowhere to go but through them.
On a boss
Medium stance. A boulder can be caught with Telekinesis for a Duet.
Sound
Roots tearing and stone grinding as it comes up, a groan while you hold it, a long throw, a dense wet thud.
[Subject 2, in the Precursors' own notes. They wrote that she lifted the test chamber. They didn't write that she was trying to get out of it.]
Shockwave
Active · Starter
Good, needs a hook
Today

A stomp and a cone out to 9 blocks. A good starter with a proper stomp. The wave itself is only light running along the ground.

After

The wave travels through the real surface. Blocks ripple and climb slopes as it passes, and you can watch it go. The crest at the far end hits hardest and throws foes up.

Where it shines
Use it on a slope or in a tight group. Whatever the far edge of the wave catches goes up in the air, and anything thrown into a wall takes a second hit.
On a boss
Light stance. Small things are left Lifted.
Sound
Keep the authored stomp. Add a low rolling rumble that moves away from you and knocks once for each foe it meets.
[Greta Moss stamped her foot at her brother in a kitchen in the old town. They found the kitchen in the next street.]
Brace
Active
Flat
Today

Three seconds at 60% less damage and no knockback, and melee attackers take a share back. It pays you to stand still, and the Arms guard now does that job better.

After

A parry with your whole body. Press as a blow arrives and you stop it dead: the hit is soaked up and thrown back as a wave when you let go. Mistime it and you still get today's 60%.

Where it shines
Press it as a blow arrives and you stop it dead, the same as a parry with a blade. Miss and you still get the 60% it gives today.
On a boss
A timed Brace counts as a deflect: it opens a riposte and a Weave.
Sound
A bronze door slamming shut inside your chest. Stop a blow with it and the door booms and shakes the floor.
[Ansel Tray held a door for nine hours so the people behind it could get out. Nobody ever told him he could stop.]
Thunderclap
Active
Good, needs a hook
Today

Radius 7 lightning and a stun, one press. At this range it plays like a recoloured Ground Slam.

After

A held clap. Your hands pull apart while you hold; let go and the air breaks in a forward wedge. Everything Charged nearby goes off with it. In rain, or standing in water, it reaches twice as far.

Where it shines
Set it off with several things Charged nearby, or stand in rain or water. All of them go at once and it reaches twice as far.
On a boss
Heavy stance when clapped into a wind-up.
Sound
A dry hand-crack right at your ears, then real thunder rolling off across the land for four seconds.
[Yara Venn clapped once to get a room's attention. It worked. They rebuilt the room.]

6 powers

Dash
Movement
Good, needs a hook
Today

A fast steered dash on a 0.7 second cooldown. Reliable, and the Ascent's air dash and the Arms dodge now sit right next to it.

After

The move that goes through things. Through a foe you leave a delayed cut. Through a blow, time hitches for one beat and it counts as a perfect dodge.

Go through a blow rather than round it and it counts as a dodge, the same one your weapons use.
On a boss
Counts as a perfect dodge: 10 on its stance, and it opens a Weave.

[Lio Sandoval ran messages across Carillon for eleven years and was never once late. He died running one. It got there.]
Flow
Active
Keep and polish
Today

A time bubble, radius 18, a quarter speed for four seconds. The headline power. Mobs slow down but the world's sound doesn't.

After

Slow everything. Rain hangs, arrows hang, and every sound that starts while it runs plays lower and duller. The marks you leave all go off together when it ends.

Where it shines
Use it with a lot of things in the air: arrows, thrown rocks, your own shots. They all hang, and it all lands together when it ends.

Bosses run at half speed instead of a quarter, and their tells stretch with them.

The world's pitch falls away, your heartbeat comes up close, and time comes back in a rising rush.
[When Sera Quill was nine she fell off a roof, and she said everything went slow on the way down. She spent the rest of her life trying to get back to that second.]

After

On a boss
The same stance as whatever it repeats, halved.
Sound
Your own last sound again, thin and a little backwards.
[Pim Arlen left a room so fast that part of him stayed in it. His friends used to say goodnight to it.]

Passive

A passive that lengthens the Ascent's wall-run. It does its job and belongs with the body's moves.

Reinvented, see Always On. Your hand drags sparks along walls, your footprints burn, the run turns red when only the power is holding you up, and all its speed goes into your next hit.

Hang in the air for five seconds. Pleasant at E rank, then the Ascent gives you far better control in the air.

Flight
Movement
Flat
Today

Free flight for 10 energy plus 6 a second, unlocked at rank A. It overlaps Wings and Skyborn and has no job of its own.

After

Flight for fighting. Wings take you far. This one stops dead, strafes and turns on a coin, so you can hang in a boss room and keep moving. At top speed a boom hits what's under you.

Active
Good, needs a hook
Today

A vortex, radius 6, four seconds. Good and useful. It makes one sound at the start and nothing for the other three and a half seconds.
